author: Nayan Seth
description:
A US congressional advisory body on China said on Friday that leading Chinese artificial intelligence firms declined to meet its members during a recent Beijing visit over concerns that doing so could expose the firms to US sanctions.
But members also underscored the importance of the coming AI dialogue between Washington and Beijing.
“We were told, ‘You guys are a really scary commission, and you do hawkish anti-China things, and they’re afraid if they meet with you, they might be put on the...
title: Chinese AI firms shunned US delegation over sanctions fears, commission says

author: Khushboo Razdan,William Zheng,Dewey Sim
description:
Rising tensions over artificial intelligence are shaping the final preparations for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to the United States.
Washington and Beijing are discussing the possibility of folding a long-awaited AI dialogue into a broader economic meeting in the days before Xi meets US President Donald Trump, according to several people familiar with the arrangements.
The two leaders agreed in Beijing in May to launch an intergovernmental dialogue on AI. For months, that channel was...
title: AI fight shadows final preparations for Xi Jinping’s White House visit

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Abnormally high temperatures across the Tibetan Plateau in early winter can trigger catastrophic rainstorms in California, according to a new study revealing a previously unidentified climate connection.
In the winters of 2016-2017 and 2022-2023, record-breaking rain swept across the US state and surrounding areas, causing billions of dollars in damage and several deaths during years when drier weather was expected in the region.
A study led by researchers from the University of California, Los...
title: Study reveals link between Tibetan Plateau heat  and record rain in California

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Fresh clues are emerging about a new type of Chinese drone being developed as a long-range intelligence and surveillance platform intended to operate deep inside contested airspace.
New photographs circulated on Chinese internet forums earlier this month that appear to show the massive drone in the air, offering much clearer views of its wing shape than earlier images. The original source of the photos and exactly where they were taken have not been independently verified.
Andreas Rupprecht, a...
title: Fresh photos offer clearest view yet of China’s ‘WZ-X’ spy drone

author: Carol Yang
description:
Beijing has strongly condemned a visit to Italy by senior Taiwanese officials and lodged formal diplomatic protests with both Rome and Brussels.
Criticising the visit on Friday, foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said Beijing had submitted “serious representations against Italy and the European Union” following reports that Taiwan’s No 2 official, Hsiao Bi-khim, had arrived in Italy to attend an international forum.
“[Taiwan’s] Democratic Progressive Party authorities and individual...
title: Beijing lodges diplomatic protests over Taiwan official’s visit to Italy

author: Carol Yang
description:
Singaporean and Chinese students led the world in educational performance in 2025, according to an assessment by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development, as average scores across OECD countries reached a record low.
The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment comprised 760,000 15-year-old students across 91 countries and economies, including OECD members and partners.
This edition of the survey was the largest since the OECD first administered the triennial...
title: Singapore and mainland China top global student assessment as OECD scores hit record low

author: Shi Huang
description:
Deng Yu, the 37-year-old Chinese mathematician who won the 2026 Fields Medal, has a backup plan if artificial intelligence puts him out of a job.
On Tuesday, he wrote on social media that “if AI can solve all maths problems, I’ll go home and write my yuri novel”.
Deng is known to be a big fan of yuri, a genre of Japanese novels and comics that depicts intimate friendships and romantic relationships between women.
In the post, which was later shared on another Chinese social platform, Deng wrote...
title: I’ll write romance novels if AI solves all maths problems, Chinese Fields winner jokes

author: Raymond Ma,Neil Denslow
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping is heading to India for the first time since 2019 and finalising plans for a US trip as he works through his busiest month of international travel in years.
Xi will attend the annual Brics summit in New Delhi over the weekend and meet Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Russia’s Vladimir Putin and South Africa’s Cyril Ramaphosa are among other leaders going to the event, which gathers some of the world’s biggest energy producers and users.
The India trip gives Xi...
title: Xi in India, bank capital injections, EU-China trade

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Battle-testing modern weapon systems can come at a steep price: a country must send its forces to war. But for China’s 4.5-generation J-10CE fighter aircraft, exports have opened another route.
Pakistan provided the aircraft’s first major combat test during its four-day conflict with India in May 2025, when Islamabad’s J-10CEs were used in an air battle. Two US officials told Reuters that at least two Indian aircraft were downed, including a French-built Rafale – though the precise losses,...
title: From Pakistan to Uzbekistan: how China’s J-10CE is widening its overseas reach

author: Laura Zhou
description:
The United States is leaning on its coastguard to reinforce its presence in the West Pacific as its navy comes under increasing strain in the Middle East.
Although this move may be seen as a lower-risk way of countering Beijing’s growing presence in the region, increasing US cooperation with the Taiwanese coastguard risks further mainland Chinese pressure on the island.
Recently, the US announced that six fast-response cutters that had been based in the Middle East for more than 20 years would...
title: US coastguards sail into troubled waters with mission to counter China in Pacific

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
US President Donald Trump and Vice-President J.D. Vance wrapped up the Republican Party’s first-ever midterm convention on Thursday night with promises of an America “greater than ever before”, aiming to secure crucial swing voters ahead of November’s battle for Congress.
“You got to get out and vote, and you got to pretend I’m on the ballot,” Trump said, while also getting the crowd at the Dallas gathering – dubbed “Trump-a-palooza” by his supporters – to pledge allegiance to him.
“You know...
title: Vance takes centre stage as Trump wraps up GOP midterm convention with voter warnings

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven stories from this week’s news across Hong Kong, mainland China, the wider Asia region and beyond that resonated with our readers and shed light on topical issues. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Beijing tells Manila to ‘stop lying’ after minister exposes South China Sea note
China has accused Philippine officials of “grandstanding and lying” after Manila’s defence secretary publicly read aloud a Chinese diplomat’s note on the...
title: Manila exposes South China Sea note; Chinese coal mine farming plan: SCMP’s 7 highlights

author: Liu Zhen
description:
The Chinese military appeared to fire flares near a Philippine aircraft operating close to the Subi and Mischief Reefs, according to the Philippines’ coastguard, as tensions continue to spread to other South China Sea hotspots.
The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) released video clips on Thursday of footage which it said had been filmed from the aircraft on Monday.
PCG spokesman Jay Tarriela said on social media that the unarmed plane was on a maritime domain awareness flight over part of the...
title: South China Sea: Manila says flares fired at aircraft near Subi, Mischief Reefs

author: Mark Magnier
description:
A survey of potential Chinese-American voters suggests a significant gender gap in party affiliation as well as a high level of willingness to vote across party lines, according to results released on Thursday.
The data – from the Committee of 100 (C100), a civic group of prominent Chinese-Americans, and a University of Chicago polling firm – challenges the common perception that these citizens form a reliable voting bloc for the Democratic Party.
Recently naturalised immigrants are more likely...
title: ‘Cross-party voting’: how Chinese-American voters are bucking the trends
